spec.description: Two intersecting chords; redundant vertex letters omitted under the house convention.
spec.mathematics: One chord has segments 12 and 4; the other has segments 6 and x.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown are visible.

answer.worked:
The products of the segments of intersecting chords are equal.
$$\begin{align*}6x&=12\times4\\6x&=48\\x&=8\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Near-vertical chord crossed by a rising chord; redundant vertex letters omitted.
spec.mathematics: The near-vertical chord has segments x and x; the crossing chord has segments 12 and 3.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown are visible.

answer.worked:
The products of the segments of intersecting chords are equal.
$$\begin{align*}x\times x&=12\times3\\x^2&=36\\x&=6\end{align*}$$
Take the positive value because $x$ is a length.

spec.description: Two crossing chords; redundant vertex letters omitted.
spec.mathematics: One chord has segments 3 and x; the other has segments 4 and 7.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown are visible.

answer.worked:
The products of the segments of intersecting chords are equal.
$$\begin{align*}3x&=4\times7\\3x&=28\\x&=\frac{28}{3}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Horizontal secant and true tangent from one external point; redundant vertex letters omitted.
spec.mathematics: External secant portion 4, internal portion 5, tangent x.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and x are visible.

answer.worked:
By the tangent and secant theorem,
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=4(4+5)\\x^2&=36\\x&=6.\end{align*}$$
The positive root is required because $x$ is a length.

spec.description: External point below the circle, left tangent and rising secant; intersections and tangency derived from the circle.
spec.mathematics: Tangent 8; external secant portion 4; internal portion x.

answer.worked:
By the tangent and secant theorem,
$$\begin{align*}4(4+x)&=8^2\\4+x&=16\\x&=12.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Secant through the marked centre and true tangent; centre marker uses ordinary black.
spec.mathematics: Radius x, external secant 3, tangent 6; internal secant is a diameter.
spec.answerVisibility: No derived diameter length is shown.

answer.worked:
The secant passes through the centre, so its internal portion is $2x$. By the tangent and secant theorem,
$$\begin{align*}3(3+2x)&=6^2\\3+2x&=12\\2x&=9\\x&=\frac92.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two secants from a common external point, with exact circle intersections; redundant vertex labels omitted.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens only; schematic lengths are not to scale.

spec.description: Steep and shallow secants from an external point below-left, with exact circle intersections.
spec.mathematics: One secant has external and internal portions x and x; the other has 4 and 14.

answer.worked:
By the secant product rule,
$$\begin{align*}x(x+x)&=4(4+14)\\2x^2&=72\\x^2&=36\\x&=6.\end{align*}$$
The positive root is required because $x$ is a length.

spec.description: Two secants with both internal portions labelled 7; exact circle intersections.
spec.mathematics: External portions x and 3; internal portions both 7.

answer.worked:
By the secant product rule,
$$\begin{align*}x(x+7)&=3(3+7)\\x^2+7x-30&=0\\(x+10)(x-3)&=0.\end{align*}$$
Thus $x=-10$ or $x=3$. Since $x$ is a length, $x=3$.

spec.description: Two intersecting chords; all four intercept labels preserved, redundant vertex letters omitted.
spec.mathematics: Intercept pairs x+5 and x, 6 and 4; schematic figure is not to scale.

answer.worked:
By the intersecting chords theorem,
$$\begin{align*}x(x+5)&=6\times4\\x^2+5x-24&=0\\(x+8)(x-3)&=0.\end{align*}$$
Thus $x=-8$ or $x=3$. Since $x$ is a length, $x=3$.

spec.description: True tangent on the left and secant through the circle from a lower external point.
spec.mathematics: Tangent 6; external secant portion 4; internal portion x.

answer.worked:
By the tangent and secant theorem,
$$\begin{align*}4(4+x)&=6^2\\4+x&=9\\x&=5.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Horizontal diameter secant and oblique secant from a common external point; exact intersections and centre retained.
spec.mathematics: Oblique external/internal portions 6 and 2; horizontal external portion x; radius 4.

answer.worked:
The diameter is $2\times4=8$. By the secant product rule,
$$\begin{align*}x(x+8)&=6(6+2)\\x^2+8x-48&=0\\(x+12)(x-4)&=0.\end{align*}$$
Thus $x=-12$ or $x=4$. Since $x$ is a length, $x=4$.
